interval.method: Split conformal absolute residual interval, marginal 90% target coverage
interval.limitation: Marginal coverage under exchangeability; not a guarantee for a particular home or under shift.

exclusions: No installation flags/dates as consumption predictors
No income, tax or deprivation proxies
No random splitting of annual observations across households
interpretation: Retrospective 2024 population-conditional expectation, not a future bill or causal retrofit prediction. Property metadata reflects the 2025 stock; renovations and survivorship may bias historic alignment.

causal_viability.decision: Use official NEED impact estimates, not a locally claimed causal effect
reasons: Public installation flags record government schemes, not all private works; zero is not untreated.
Dates are latest recorded installation; prior interventions and treatment histories are incomplete.
Occupancy, income, household changes and treatment assignment are not observed; parallel trends/exchangeability cannot be established.
Current EPC and property attributes are undated/post-treatment. Matching or heterogeneous causal effects would be confounded.

selection.selection_basis: Fresh development validation only; A legacy validation reproduction separate; old reported test never queried
selection.final_policy: Property deployment challenger: validation Pareto improvement in both MAE and R² over A, then lowest MAE among feasible candidates. History selection: validation Pareto/MAE versus persistence and comparisons restricted to its information cohort. Final deployment requires improvement on the fresh final set and paired group-bootstrap evidence for MAE, feature availability, interval coverage and subgroup checks.
selection.deployment_context: B_default uses the existing four inputs, with pooled terrace type. B is a richer reported-subtype experiment; no silent provision of true subtype for default inference. Optional subtype deployment requires its own predeclared improvement gate.

deployment_gates.default: Both final MAE and R² improve over A; paired property-group bootstrap MAE gain 95% CI strictly positive; required inputs unchanged. Report every subgroup, and retain baseline for unsupported cells.
deployment_gates.detail: Optional detail model must improve final MAE and R² over default for terrace rows with reported subtype; paired-group MAE CI strictly positive. Otherwise keep detail as research only.
deployment_gates.history: Separate optional source-year scenario. C must improve both final MAE and R² over persistence on the identical history-eligible cohort, with positive paired-group MAE gain CI. Require matching weather-corrected historical inputs; never relabel this as property-only performance.

limitations: Final property holdout is independent of the known 50,000-row groups, but drawn from the same 2026 release.
Current property snapshots are retrospective; EPC and mutable undated fields remain excluded.
Historical readings are revised/weather-corrected source-year figures; ordinary raw bills and real-time vintages are not validated.
C has different information and an eligibility subset; it is never reported as default-model performance.
